entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6362"/><div sID="gen9748" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6362"/>2. his importunacy.<div eID="gen9748" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9749" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my sore ran ... night--</hi>literally, "my hand was spread," or, "stretched out" (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.44.20">Psa 44:20</reference>).<div eID="gen9749" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9750" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">ceased not--</hi>literally, "grew not numb," or, "feeble" (<reference osisRef="Gen.45.26">Ge 45:26</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.38.8">Psa 38:8</reference>).<div eID="gen9750" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9751" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my soul ... comforted--</hi>(compare <reference osisRef="Gen.37.35">Ge 37:35</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jer.31.15">Jr 31:15</reference>). <div eID="gen9751" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 2. his importunacy. my sore ran ... night-- literally, "my hand was spread," or, "stretched out" (compare Psa 44:20 ). ceased not-- literally, "grew not numb," or, "feeble" ( Ge 45:26 ; Psa 38:8 ). my soul ... comforted-- (compare Ge 37:35 ; Jr 31:15 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6363"/><div sID="gen9752" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6363"/>3-9. His sad state contrasted with former joys.<div eID="gen9752" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9753" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">was troubled--</hi>literally, "violently agitated," or disquieted (<reference osisRef="Ps.39.6">Psa 39:6</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.41.5">41:5</reference>).<div eID="gen9753" type="x-p"/> <div sID="gen9754" type="x-p"/><hi type="bold">my spirit was overwhelmed--</hi>or, "fainted" (<reference osisRef="Ps.107.5">Psa 107:5</reference>; <reference osisRef="Jonah.2.7">Jon 2:7</reference>). <div eID="gen9754" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 3-9. His sad state contrasted with former joys. was troubled-- literally, "violently agitated," or disquieted ( Psa 39:6 ; 41:5 ). my spirit was overwhelmed-- or, "fainted" ( Psa 107:5 ; Jon 2:7 ).

Omitting the supplied words, we may read, "This is my affliction--</hi>the years of," &c., "years" being taken as parallel to affliction (compare <reference osisRef="Ps.90.15">Psa 90:15</reference>), as of God's ordering. <div eID="gen9756" type="x-p"/>

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6366"/><div sID="gen9757" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6366"/>11-12. He finds relief in contrasting God's former deliverances. Shall we receive good at His hands, and not evil? Both are orderings of unerring mercy and unfailing love. <div eID="gen9757" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 11-12. He finds relief in contrasting God's former deliverances. Shall we receive good at His hands, and not evil? Both are orderings of unerring mercy and unfailing love.

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6367"/><div sID="gen9758" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6367"/><hi type="bold">13. Thy way ... in the sanctuary--</hi>God's ways of grace and providence (<reference osisRef="Ps.22.3">Psa 22:3</reference>; <reference osisRef="Ps.67.2">67:2</reference>), ordered on holy principles, as developed in His worship; or implied in His perfections, if "holiness" be used for "sanctuary," as some prefer translating (compare <reference osisRef="Exod.15.11">Ex 15:11</reference>). <div eID="gen9758" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 13. Thy way ... in the sanctuary-- God's ways of grace and providence ( Psa 22:3 ; 67:2 ), ordered on holy principles, as developed in His worship; or implied in His perfections, if "holiness" be used for "sanctuary," as some prefer translating (compare Ex 15:11 ).
entries.reader_content_plain: 13. Thy way ... in the sanctuary-- God's ways of grace and providence ( Psa 22:3 ; 67:2 ), ordered on holy principles, as developed in His worship; or implied in His perfections, if "holiness" be used for "sanctuary," as some prefer translating (compare Ex 15:11 ).

entries.content_osis: <div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" sID="pv6368"/><div sID="gen9759" type="x-p"/><div type="x-milestone" subType="x-preverse" eID="pv6368"/>14-20. Illustrations of God's power in His special interventions for His people (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.1-Exod.14.31">Ex 14:1-31</reference>), and, in the more common, but sublime, control of nature (<reference osisRef="Ps.22.11-Ps.22.14">Psa 22:11-14</reference>; <reference osisRef="Hab.3.14">Ha 3:14</reference>) which may have attended those miraculous events (<reference osisRef="Exod.14.24">Ex 14:24</reference>). <div eID="gen9759" type="x-p"/>
entries.content_plain: 14-20. Illustrations of God's power in His special interventions for His people ( Ex 14:1-31 ), and, in the more common, but sublime, control of nature ( Psa 22:11-14 ; Ha 3:14 ) which may have attended those miraculous events ( Ex 14:24 ).
entries.reader_content_plain: 14-20. Illustrations of God's power in His special interventions for His people ( Ex 14:1-31 ), and, in the more common, but sublime, control of nature ( Psa 22:11-14 ; Ha 3:14 ) which may have attended those miraculous events ( Ex 14:24 ).
